udd08db85a3: For a batch of Bluetooth products based on the same chip, the goal is for the Bluetooth address of every chip to fall within a specified address range, with each chip having a unique Bluetooth address. To achieve this, when updating the fw programming firmware, configure the corresponding Bluetooth address range in the programming options of the PC tool; while the target chip firmware is being programmed, the Bluetooth addresses are programmed into a specified location in each chip in incrementing order, so that the Bluetooth address programmed into the chip can be used in SDK development. In addition, in SDK development, the Bluetooth address can be appended to the Bluetooth name in a specified format, making the Bluetooth name unique.
uf8f7220b5f: In the control panel for updating the target chip firmware, after opening and selecting the target chip fw file to be programmed, proceed as shown in ⟦1⟧Bluetooth address auto-increment configuration⟦/1⟧:
u52a158afbe: [1] Check "Update Bluetooth address" (更新蓝牙地址) (if unchecked, the SDK uses a randomly assigned Bluetooth address);
u9bbba641e4: [2] Enter the Bluetooth address auto-increment range;
u3d20f7c7c2: [3] Choose whether to check "Overwrite Bluetooth address" (覆盖蓝牙地址) (if checked, a chip that already has a Bluetooth address is overwritten with a new address; to avoid waste, it is generally left unchecked);
uf8cad57033: [4] Click Deploy (部署) to update the fw file and configuration information to the programmer;
ud7d0a04ebc: The address range set each time must not exceed the u32 range. Otherwise, the error [Bluetooth address initialization failed] (蓝牙地址初始化失败) may be reported
u2691ff6c50: Bluetooth addresses are programmed in incrementing order, starting from the lowest address in the address range configured in the programming options. While programming the chip firmware, the programmer also programs the Bluetooth address into the target chip.
u9b5cc9d6cb: For example, if the Bluetooth address range is set to ⟦1⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 : 01 - 00: 00 : 00 :FF : FF : FF⟦/1⟧, the Bluetooth address of the first chip after successful programming is ⟦2⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :01⟦/2⟧, that of the second chip is ⟦3⟧00: 00 : 00 :00 : 00 :02⟦/3⟧, and so on. After all addresses in the set range have been programmed, the programmer reports "Bluetooth addresses used up" (蓝牙地址已用完) and can no longer program firmware. ua852865b7f: Keeping the chip's existing Bluetooth address when reprogramming
u32563ce7a2: In some scenarios, chips that have already been programmed with a Bluetooth address need to keep their existing Bluetooth address when they are reprogrammed with new firmware. There are usually the following two cases.
u6999f76812: Bluetooth address in the chip's FLASH programmed by a 1-to-2 or 1-to-8 programmer
u8e0a059bb3: If the Bluetooth address in the chip's FLASH was programmed from a specified range using a 1-to-2 or 1-to-8 programmer, the location of the Bluetooth address is fixed.
u53b297a743: Select [Sequential auto-increment] (顺序自增) to keep the address. With this method, if the Bluetooth address already in the chip's FLASH is within the set range, it is not erased but kept during reprogramming; if it is not within the set range, it is erased and a new address is written. Before programming, you can first spot-check some chips to see the previously programmed Bluetooth address values. Suppose the Bluetooth address of a spot-checked chip is 85:A6:33:43:87:E4 and the first two bytes of the other devices all start with 85 A6; you can then configure the Bluetooth address range as 85:A6:00:00:00:00 ~ 85:A6:FF:FF:FF:FF. As long as the Bluetooth address of the device's chip is within the set address range during reprogramming, it is not erased. The precondition is that the first two bytes of all devices must be identical, so that a range containing the devices' Bluetooth addresses can easily be set for reprogramming while keeping the existing Bluetooth addresses in the chips. This restriction exists mainly because the auto-increment counter is only 4 bytes long.
uc7debd8016: Select [Retain auto-increment] (保留自增) to keep the address. With this method, the address in the FLASH is not erased during reprogramming, regardless of whether the Bluetooth address already in the chip's FLASH is within the set auto-increment range; if the chip's FLASH contains no address, an address from the set range is programmed into the chip.
u94322ecab9: Random address generated automatically by the SDK
u4b6d76d429: Depending on the chip model, the Bluetooth address generated automatically by the application may be stored in the VM area or in the bt_info area. To keep the existing Bluetooth address in the chip's FLASH during reprogramming, you cannot use the sequential auto-increment or retain auto-increment methods described above; instead, uncheck the [Erase entire FLASH before programming] (烧写前擦除整个FLASH) and [Erase VM] (擦除VM) options, and also make sure that the FW to be reprogrammed has the same VM address as the firmware already programmed into the chip (if the Bluetooth address is stored in bt_info, also make sure that this configured address is the same). After reprogramming, whether the address has been kept must be confirmed by actual testing.
u81939df725: The 1-to-8 programmer has a built-in current test module that can measure the current drawn by the loads on its 8 USB programming ports. The current and power consumption test function is mainly used to measure the device's current in various situations, in order to screen out chips whose current values do not meet the requirements in each situation.
u7c876b30b4: The 1-to-8 programmer supports testing chip power consumption while programming the chip firmware. It can test the device's power consumption in 4 situations: power-on (the moment the device starts being programmed), startup (the device simulates startup), standby (the chip enters standby mode) and shutdown (the chip enters shutdown mode).
uf9580efb80: A standalone current test function is also supported, which can test the device's static current (while powered) and shutdown current (in soft shutdown mode).
ufc1748f7b1: Using the combined programming and power consumption test
u092ea83fe5: The combined programming and power consumption test function is currently supported on the 1-to-8 programmer only for the AC897N and AD697N chips. If you need this test for other models, consult Jieli technical support.
ud1405903f1: [1] In the control panel for updating the target chip firmware, open and select the target chip firmware to be programmed;
ue0d7aa3645: [2] Select and configure the current test items as shown in ⟦1⟧Current test item configuration⟦/1⟧ (do not set the values too small: the measured current depends heavily on the device's hardware circuit, and the programmer's test accuracy and stability are not very high, so it can only screen out chips with obviously abnormal power consumption);
ud428dc473c: [3] Update the firmware and configuration information to the programmer;
ue59c9fabc4: [4] During chip firmware programming, the selected power-on, startup, standby and shutdown current tests are performed. If a measured current value is greater than the set maximum, the programmer reports a current error;
u95feefba5c: For the standalone current test, the static current test supports chips of any model, while the shutdown current test is currently supported on the 1-to-8 programmer only for the AC897N, AD697N and AD698N chips. If you need this test for other chip models, consult Jieli technical support.

uc43910c035: In the static current test, the programmer works like an ammeter: it measures the current consumed by the device while the USB programming interface supplies power to it. As shown in ⟦1⟧Static current test⟦/1⟧, after the device is connected to a USB programming channel of the programmer, the programmer display shows the device's current consumption in real time. If the current exceeds the set threshold for more than 8S, the programmer reports an error. If the device's instantaneous current exceeds 160mA, the programmer cuts off power to the USB port and reports an error; the programmer must then be restarted before testing can continue.
